itineraries.title: Manali and Kasol in 5 days

itineraries.title: Dharamshala and Dalhousie in 5 days
itineraries.summary: Tibetan McLeodganj and the Triund ridge, then west to colonial Dalhousie for Khajjiar's meadow and a day in old Chamba.
itineraries.seoTitle: Dharamshala and Dalhousie in 5 Days with Khajjiar
itineraries.seoDescription: 5-day Kangra–Chamba itinerary with official drive times, altitudes and stays: McLeodganj, Triund, Dalhousie, Khajjiar, Dainkund and Chamba.

plan.overview: For a quieter trip below the Dhauladhar: Tibetan culture and an easy-to-moderate trek, then old hill stations and meadows. Fly into Gaggal (Kangra), 23 km from McLeodganj, and leave from Pathankot, 86 km from Dalhousie. The one long drive is Day 3 — Dharamshala to Dalhousie is 120 km, about four hours. March to June is best; Dharamshala is one of the wettest places in the state from June to mid-September.
plan.style: Hill stations · culture · one easy trek

itineraries.seoTitle: Shimla and Manali in 6 Days: Toy Train to Solang
itineraries.seoDescription: 6-day Shimla–Manali itinerary with official drive times, stays, fees and season: Kalka–Shimla toy train, Jakhoo, Kullu, Manali, Solang and the Atal Tunnel.

plan.overview: For first-timers and families who want the two best-known hill towns. It starts at Kalka (or Chandigarh, 115 km below Shimla) and ends at Manali, so you fly out of Bhuntar or take the overnight Volvo to Delhi. Day 3 is the long one — Shimla to Manali is 236 km, about seven and a half hours by HPTDC's count — so leave early. Both towns sit at about 2,000–2,400 m, so altitude is not a concern. Avoid July–August if you can: roads are slippery, landslides happen, and adventure sports stop from 15 July to 15 September.

Going in from Shimla lets you climb slowly — Shimla (about 2,376 m), Kalpa (about 2,960 m), Nako (about 3,625 m) — before Kaza (about 3,650 m) and the Key–Kibber–Langza villages above 4,000 m. Going the other way, Manali (about 2,050 m) to Kaza is one five-hour drive over Kunzum Pass at 4,551 m. Plan the full loop for June to October: the Shimla–Kinnaur–Kaza road is open all year, but the Manali side is shut for about seven winter months and its buses run only July to October. Signal is thin — in Spiti only BSNL works well — and foreign visitors need an Inner Line Permit for some inner areas.

plan.transport: A sturdy off-road taxi or your own high-clearance vehicle is recommended. Regular buses also run Shimla–Kinnaur–Kaza (May–October) and Manali–Kaza (July–October).

prep.body: Spiti is cold all year: May and June reach only about 15–20°C, and December–February can fall to −20°C. Pack woollens on every trip.

faqs.q: Should I start from Shimla or Manali?
faqs.a: From Shimla, if you can. That side climbs over several days — Shimla about 2,376 m, Kalpa about 2,960 m, Nako about 3,625 m — while Manali (about 2,050 m) to Kaza crosses Kunzum Pass at 4,551 m in a single five-hour drive.

faqs.q: Can I do the Spiti circuit in winter?
faqs.a: Not the full loop. The Manali–Kaza road over Kunzum is shut for about seven winter months, though the Kaza–Tabo–Pooh–Shimla road stays open all year. Spiti can fall to −20°C in December–February, and HPTDC's hotels at Kalpa and Kaza close for winter.

faqs.q: Is there public transport?
faqs.a: Yes, in season: regular buses run Shimla–Kinnaur–Kaza from May to October and Manali–Kaza from July to October.

faqs.q: Will my phone work?
faqs.a: In Spiti only BSNL works well and internet is slow. Kinnaur has good signal at Reckong Peo, Kalpa and Sangla.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit?
faqs.a: Foreign tourists need an Inner Line Permit for some inner areas of Kinnaur and Spiti near the Tibet border. It is issued in New Delhi (Himachal Bhawan), Shimla, Reckong Peo and at SDM offices in Kalpa, Kaza and Manali.

faqs.q: When is Chandratal open?
faqs.a: From late May to early October. Its road branches off about 2.9 km from Batal and 8 km from Kunzum Pass.

faqs.q: How long is the drive from Shimla to Kaza?
faqs.a: 419 km, about 12 hours' driving by HPTDC's count — this plan spreads it over five days.

sections.heading: By air
sections.text: Five airports serve the state: Chandigarh and Pathankot on its borders, and Gaggal-Kangra, Bhuntar-Kullu and Jubbarhatti-Shimla inside it. Gaggal and Pathankot are for Kangra, Dharamshala and Chamba; Bhuntar for Kullu, Manali, Mandi and Lahaul-Spiti; Chandigarh and Jubbarhatti for Shimla, Solan and Kinnaur. Bhuntar has flights to Delhi and Chandigarh; daily flights from Delhi land at Jubbarhatti; Gaggal has regular flights from Delhi.

sections.heading: By train
sections.text: Broad-gauge trains reach Kalka and Pathankot. From Kalka, the 96 km narrow-gauge line to Shimla — opened in 1903 and part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site — is a journey in itself. From Pathankot a narrow-gauge line runs through the Kangra valley to Joginder Nagar, passing Kangra station, 20 km from Dharamshala, and Ahju, 3 km from Bir. There is no railway to Manali.

sections.heading: By bus
sections.text: Interstate buses run from Delhi, Chandigarh, Jaipur and other nearby cities. Ordinary and luxury coaches link Delhi and Chandigarh with Shimla and Kullu, and deluxe and AC Volvo buses run to Manali — booking ahead is recommended. Within the state, public transport and taxis serve every destination.

guides.title: Himachal in the monsoon: where to go in July–September and what to avoid
guides.summary: What the July–September rains change in Himachal — landslide-prone roads, closed adventure sports — and where the season shines: dry Spiti and Lahaul, waterfalls and the Minjar fair.
guides.seoTitle: Himachal in the Monsoon: Roads, Spiti and Waterfalls
guides.seoDescription: Travelling in Himachal from July to September: landslides and road safety, the 15 July–15 September adventure closure, dry Spiti and Lahaul, waterfalls and monsoon fairs.

body.intro: The monsoon turns Himachal's lower valleys green and fills its waterfalls, but it also brings the year's worst roads. Plan around it rather than through it: here is what changes and where to go instead.

items.body: In July and August roads are slippery and landslides and rock-falls happen — drive with care and keep to the left.
items.title: Roads

items.body: Rafting, river crossing and paragliding stop from 15 July to 15 September.
items.title: Adventure sports

items.body: Don't stand on cliff edges or riverside boulders — the rivers are strong and deceptive.

sections.heading: Where it stays dry: Spiti and Lahaul
sections.text: Spiti and Lahaul sit in the rain shadow and are cold and almost rainless. This is their season: buses run from Shimla via Kinnaur from May to October and from Manali from July to October, and Kaza's Ladarcha trade fair is held in July/August.

sections.heading: How to plan
sections.text: Keep a spare day on any long road journey, travel in daylight and avoid planning rafting or paragliding between mid-July and mid-September. If you want the mountains without the rain, go to Spiti and Lahaul.

guides.title: Snow in Himachal: where and when to see it
guides.summary: When and where snow falls in Himachal — Manali and Solang, the Kullu valley, Dharamshala, Dalhousie and Kalatop, Shimla's ice rink — plus winter road closures and how cold it gets.
guides.seoTitle: Snow in Himachal: Best Places and Months
guides.seoDescription: Where to see snow in Himachal and when: Manali and Solang (December–March), Kullu, Dharamshala, Dalhousie, Shimla's ice skating, Rohtang closures and Spiti's −20°C.

body.intro: Snow is the main reason many people come to Himachal in winter. It falls at different times in different places, and the highest roads close, so match the place to the month.

items.body: Snow falls mainly from December to early March; December–January can drop below −5°C.

sections.heading: Roads in winter
sections.text: Heavy snow closes Rohtang Pass in late November and it reopens around May. The Atal Tunnel keeps Lahaul reachable from Manali, and Sissu is about 40 km away — but check locally, as its panchayat has at times paused tourist activities. Spiti can fall to −20°C in winter.

sections.heading: Stay safe
sections.text: Mountain weather changes fast, so carry woollens even on a sunny day, drive slowly on hill roads and use only licensed operators for skiing.
